solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Private place, in time, is moderate

indicators.note: the private place sits within the word for time, so 'in' asks for one piece inside the other

parts.note: a day is a period of time
own, as in one's own private affairs
PL is the standard abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: Someone's private spot, visited at the right moment, turns out to be quite modest.
explanation.definitionFit: To play something down is to moderate or minimise its importance; both are verbs.

clue.text: Storage unit's opened correctly, but not intelligently

indicators.note: the storage unit has opened the word for correctly, splitting it to sit inside

parts.note: duly means properly or correctly
MB, megabyte, is a unit of computer storage

explanation.surface: A storage unit was opened properly, though without much thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumbly can mean stupidly, so it is a synonym of unintelligently.

clue.text: Strong breeze around that's turbulent weather

indicators.note: around says the breeze encircles the other letters

parts.note: a strong breeze is wind

indicators.note: turbulent means agitated, so these letters are churned

explanation.surface: A forecast of strong wind and turbulent weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strong breeze' looks like part of a forecast but is just the wind; 'weather' is the verb meaning to come through a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: To weather a storm is to withstand it; both are verbs of enduring.

clue.text: Claim of 17 28 yet this worried us

parts.note: the answer to 28 means proper, accepted as correct

indicators.note: worried means stirred up, so these letters are agitated

parts.note: the setter speaks for the Financial Times, so us is FT

explanation.surface: A thinker's assertion was accepted, yet it alarmed the paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges YET THIS into TYISTHE. 17 is the French socialist Proudhon, whose famous slogan this is.
explanation.definitionFit: Proudhon declared this in What Is Property?, his famous anarchist assertion.

clue.text: Act against what monarch has heard

indicators.note: heard means the phrase is spoken and its sound matters

parts.note: a monarch has a reign

explanation.surface: Taking action against what a king is rumoured to have.
explanation.definitionFit: To arraign is to indict or accuse formally, to act against someone in court.

clue.text: Mineral paste to stop spot returning

indicators.note: the turned word plugs the paste like a stopper, so it goes inside

parts.note: gum is an adhesive paste

indicators.note: returning tells us the word for spot comes back, read right to left

parts.note: to spot is to spy, to catch sight of

explanation.surface: Applying a mineral paste to keep a pimple from coming back.
explanation.definitionFit: Gypsum is a soft calcium sulphate mineral used to make plaster.

definitions.meaning: a polite protest on being given a present, matching the thanks of 19
a reply to the slogan of 3, since if property is theft ... taken it

explanation.walkthrough: 19 is THANKS and 3 is PROPERTY IS THEFT; the phrase answers each.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said to a gift-giver and also as a rebuke to a taker.

clue.text: Exclusive small grocery store

parts.note: the Co-op is a British chain of grocery stores

explanation.surface: A small corner shop sells only one product.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoop is an exclusive news story that a paper gets first.

clue.text: Mouth's capacity to expand

parts.note: mush is slang for the mouth or face
room is space or capacity

explanation.surface: The mouth's ability to stretch open.
explanation.definitionFit: To mushroom is to grow rapidly, a verb of expansion.

clue.text: Energy contained by double plug

indicators.note: contained by puts the energy word inside the other

parts.note: a spit is a double, as in the spit of someone
go means energy or drive

explanation.surface: Energy held in check by a twin plug.
explanation.definitionFit: A spigot is a peg or plug for stopping the vent of a cask.

clue.text: Coaster from Australia brought back some bread

parts.note: a coaster is a little mat for a drink

indicators.note: brought back says the short word for Australia is turned round

parts.note: Oz is the informal name for Australia

explanation.surface: A drinks coaster and some bread brought home from a trip Down Under.
explanation.definitionFit: Matzo is the flat unleavened bread eaten at Passover.

clue.text: Moving up, our star over the moon

indicators.note: moving suggests the letters shift about into a new order

explanation.surface: A celebrity on the rise is delighted with their success.
explanation.definitionFit: Over the moon is an idiom for delighted, matching ecstatic or enraptured.

clue.text: Funny tingles in all ears

indicators.note: funny means odd or peculiar, so the letters come out strangely arranged

explanation.surface: A strange tingling sensation felt in both ears.
explanation.definitionFit: Being all ears is an idiom for paying full attention to what is said.

clue.text: They appear regularly excited

indicators.note: regularly asks for every second letter of the words that follow it

explanation.surface: They show up excited, as if on schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyper is informal for overexcited or highly strung.

clue.text: Roman statesman's restricted by new printer

indicators.note: restricted means held in, so the statesman's name surrounds the letter for 'by'

parts.note: Cato the Elder was a Roman statesman; the possessive gives no letter
X is the multiplication sign, read as 'by' (three by four)

explanation.surface: A Roman politician is hemmed in by a new printing press operator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' looks like a link word but is the piece: X as in 'times', placed inside CATO.
explanation.definitionFit: William Caxton introduced the printing press to England in the fifteenth century.

clue.text: Bird has to visit a business

parts.note: to tour a place is to visit it
Co is the abbreviation for company, a business

explanation.surface: A bird needs to call on a firm.
explanation.definitionFit: The touraco, or turaco, is a brightly coloured African bird.

clue.text: A sport's significance for defender

parts.note: polo is a sport; the possessive gives no letter
the gist is the essential meaning

explanation.surface: A game's meaning matters to a defensive player.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologist defends a cause or belief in argument.

clue.text: Love to support immodest socialist

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting word sits underneath

parts.note: proud can mean conceited, immodest
hon, short for honey, is a term of endearment like love

explanation.surface: Affection backs a vain left-winger.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre-Joseph Proudhon was a nineteenth-century French socialist and anarchist thinker.

clue.text: Heads off old-timers confused in heat of battle?

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so what is left is rearranged
heads off removes the leading letters, here the O and L that open the hyphenated word

explanation.surface: Veterans lose their heads in confusion when the fighting gets fierce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads off' takes O and L from the front of OLD-TIMERS, leaving DTIMERS, which 'confused' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Red mist is the idiom for a surge of rage that clouds judgement, as in combat.

clue.text: Actor officially getting recognition?

definitions.meaning: the actor Tom Hanks given formally by initial and surname
gratitude or acknowledgement shown to someone

explanation.definitionFit: Thanks are expressions of gratitude, a form of recognition.

clue.text: Military bosses against one of the latest gadgets

parts.note: MoD is the UK Ministry of Defence, in charge of the armed forces
con means against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: Army chiefs set themselves against a modern gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A mod con is a modern convenience, a labour-saving domestic appliance.

clue.text: Male rock band not quite game for musical

parts.note: ELO is the Electric Light Orchestra, a rock band

indicators.note: not quite drops the last letter

parts.note: dice is a game

explanation.surface: A man's rock group is not quite right for a stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: Melodic means tuneful, having a pleasing melody.

clue.text: Better than that which fills sack

indicators.note: fills says one word goes inside the other

parts.note: the sack is slang for bed
yon is an old word for that

explanation.surface: Something superior to what goes into a sack.
explanation.definitionFit: Beyond can mean surpassing or exceeding, so better than.

clue.text: Complaint from group at university

parts.note: up means at university, as in 'up at Oxford'
a set is a group of things

explanation.surface: A grievance raised by a student society.
explanation.definitionFit: An upset is a minor illness, as in a stomach upset; both are nouns for ailments.

clue.text: Sort of boom that's very good if base is removed

indicators.note: in a down entry the base is the last letter, which goes

parts.note: so nice means very good

explanation.surface: A loud bang that would be great if the bottom fell out.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonic boom is the noise of something breaking the sound barrier.

clue.text: Divide then bind together an element

parts.note: to allot is to divide up and share out
to rope things is to tie them together

explanation.surface: Instructions to separate things and then tie them up again.
explanation.definitionFit: An allotrope is one of the physical forms an element can take, as diamond is of carbon.

clue.text: Bullied man kissed tip of proboscis

parts.note: he is a man, the male pronoun

indicators.note: tip of keeps only the leading letter of a word for the snout

parts.note: a proboscis is a nose
pecked means gave a quick light kiss

explanation.surface: A man gives a peck on the end of someone's nose.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's own parse put P inside HE NECKED for an earlier clue that was edited; as printed, read N as the tip of the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Henpecked describes someone nagged and dominated, usually by a spouse.

clue.text: Information from bible is old

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Bible as an ancient source of knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviso is an advice or notification, an old word for information sent.

clue.text: Indiscreetly loses every other shade?

indicators.note: dropping alternate letters keeps only the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: Someone who gossips drops every other colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A nicety is a fine distinction, a shade of difference.

clue.text: Worked to hold 8 in?

indicators.note: to hold means to contain, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: acted, as in performed or worked
a cep is a kind of mushroom, the answer to 8 down

explanation.surface: Was the job done with a fungus inside it?
explanation.definitionFit: In means fashionable or accepted, as something widely approved.
